text:
Marissa Cole: Mid-sprint readout thread for lifecycle experiments. Dropping early numbers + guardrails checks here so we can decide if we iterate nudge copy this week or hold.

Ben Carter: Thanks @Marissa. Quick framing: we’re ~48h post launch for email v1 + console nudges v1 + retargeting audiences. Numbers are directional (small sample) but want to catch any obvious “this is confusing users” signals.

Tyler Benson: Here’s the dashboard cut I’m using (24h activation + time-to-first-success). Looker link: https://looker.redwoodinference.com/dashboards/activation-sprint-wk1 (internal)

Tyler Benson: Snapshot since launch (self-serve new signups only; excludes invited teammates):
- Activation (first_request_success within 24h): 31.8% baseline → 35.6% current (Δ +3.8pp)
- Activation within 72h: too early to call but trending +4–5pp
- Median time-to-first-success: 22m baseline → 17m current
- Email: Welcome open 52%, click 18% (CTA to quickstart)
- Console checklist: shown to 63% of eligible users (flag rollout 50% + eligibility gating), CTR on “Create API key” step 14%, “Run first request” step 9%
Caveat: we still have some missingness on `first_streaming_success` event (see below).

Henry Cho: For decision-making, are we using 24h activation as primary (per PM-412)? Or are we still sanity-checking streaming success as “production-like” proxy?

Paula Mendes: Primary for sprint: `first_request_success` (2xx completion) within 24h/72h. We’ll report streaming + dashboard_viewed as secondary “depth” milestones. Streaming instrumentation is partially fixed but not complete for Python SDK streaming path.

Marissa Cole: +1. We shouldn’t move goalposts mid-sprint. But if copy is pushing streaming and it’s broken/under-measured, we’ll confuse ourselves.

Allison Grant: Guardrails pass so far (console):
- P95 console page load stable (dashboard route + project setup). No regression above noise.
- Error rate for checklist endpoints flat.
- No spike in client errors tied to the banner impressions.
I’m watching the “banner_render_time_ms” and “console_error_boundary” alerts — green.

Sean Gallagher: SLO/infra guardrails also green. No noticeable increase in inference errors or latency correlated with onboarding nudges.

Dev Patel: Support side: volume is slightly up but seems within expected launch noise. 6 tickets tagged “onboarding” since yesterday; 3 are “API key permissions/confusion”, 2 are “link landed me on wrong page”, 1 is “emails too frequent”. Nothing like a flood. If we tweak copy, please keep the support CTA stable so we can track.

Ben Carter: Re: “whether to iterate nudge copy” — we’re seeing a pattern in session replays / comments:
- Users click checklist “Run first request” and bounce when they hit auth error (missing header or wrong key)
- Some confusion on models: “Which model should I pick?”
Proposed: adjust checklist copy to be more explicit and point to “copy-paste curl” section.

Marissa Cole: Can we get concrete proposed strings? I don’t want to churn UI daily but small copy changes are fine.

Ben Carter: Draft changes (small):
1) Banner (top of dashboard) current: “Finish setup to get production-ready inference.”
   Proposed: “Make your first successful request (2 min). Copy/paste a curl command.”
2) Checklist step “Run your first request” helper text current: “Send a request to any model.”
   Proposed: “Send a test request (curl/SDK). We’ll validate your API key + headers.”
3) Add inline link “Common errors: 401/429/404” to troubleshooting anchor in quickstart.

Paula Mendes: If we change copy, please keep event names stable. We can add `nudge_copy_variant` property so analysis can separate v1 vs v1.1.

Jada Williams: From implementation side, copy-only is safe. We can ship via config without redeploy (the nudge framework reads from remote config). If we want `nudge_copy_variant`, that’s a tiny add but would require a console deploy. Could also encode variant in the config key and log the key name.

Tyler Benson: On measurement: checklist CTR looks decent, but the biggest drop is still between api_key_created → first_request_success. Baseline drop was ~44% and we’re at ~41% right now. Not huge but in right direction.

Henry Cho: Any sign we’re just shifting the metric (e.g., more people do a tiny hello-world but don’t come back)?

Tyler Benson: Too early for D7/D14 obviously. For “early retention proxy” we looked at repeat requests within 24h of first success: baseline 26% → 28% (small n). Not alarming.

Allison Grant: Also: dashboard_viewed is up. Could be nudges driving it, but it’s a good sign for “they saw cost/latency breakdown.”

Dev Patel: The “API key permissions/confusion” tickets: users are creating a key but then using the wrong environment (copying prod key into dev project or vice versa). If the nudge can clarify “make sure you’re in the same project,” that might remove a chunk of tickets.

Marissa Cole: That’s helpful. But we should avoid making the checklist feel heavy. Maybe helper text: “Use the key from this project.”

Ben Carter: Agree. Also, guardrail: unsubscribes. Tyler — any email unsub spike?

Tyler Benson: Unsub rate is 0.19% vs normal ~0.15%. Slightly elevated but not concerning yet. Complaint rate is below threshold. Deliverability looks fine (no domain reputation dip). Suppressions seem to be working (no obvious “opted out but still receiving” cases in the last 24h).

Paula Mendes: One more caveat: streaming event undercount. The PR fix is in, but we only rolled it to 20% on backend as of last night. So ignore streaming success delta for now.

Sean Gallagher: +1 on not using streaming for decision until instrumentation is stable. I’m fine with copy encouraging it, but only if docs path is solid.

Marissa Cole: Decision proposal:
- Keep experiment running as-is for another 48h to avoid thrash
- BUT ship a small copy update (banner + checklist helper text + troubleshooting link) as v1.1 via config today
- Add “same project key” hint if we can do it without UI changes
Any objections?

Henry Cho: No objection. If we do v1.1, let’s document in the experiment tracker with timestamp and exact strings.

Tyler Benson: Works for me. I’ll annotate dashboards with a vertical line + add to tracker.

Jada Williams: I can push config update within the hour. For `nudge_copy_variant`, easiest is to log the config key name as `nudge_template_id` (already in payload). That should be enough for slicing.

Ben Carter: Great. I’ll update the copy doc + ping Design for quick review. @Marissa can you approve final strings in-thread once posted?

Marissa Cole: Yes. Post final copy here and I’ll :thumbsup:.

Ben Carter: Final v1.1 copy:
- Banner headline: “Make your first successful request (2 min).”
- Banner subtext: “Copy/paste a curl command. We’ll help you validate your API key + headers.”
- Banner CTA: “Open Quickstart”
- Checklist step title unchanged: “Run your first request”
- Checklist helper text: “Send a test request (curl/SDK). Use the API key from this project.”
- Inline link: “Common errors (401/429/404)” → https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart#troubleshooting

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: Approved.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: from Support. The “same project” hint should help.

Tyler Benson: Noted. I’ll watch for any change in error banner clicks + support-link clicks as guardrails after the copy updates.

Allison Grant: I’ll keep an eye on console perf but config-only change shouldn’t move anything.

Marissa Cole: Cool. Let’s regroup in 2 days with updated numbers + any guardrail deltas. Please keep dropping observations in this thread as they come up.
